# inventory.sh: stock file helpers.
# Stock files are CSV: sku,name,qty,price_cents with a header line. Names may
# be quoted and contain commas. Exports from the warehouse system do not end
# with a newline.
. lib/format.sh

# each_item FILE: print "sku qty price_cents" for every data row
each_item() {
  local sku name qty price
  {
    read -r _header
    while IFS=, read -r sku name qty price; do
      echo "$sku $qty $price"
    done
  } < "$1"
}

# total_value FILE: sum of qty*price_cents over all rows, formatted as dollars
total_value() {
  local total=0 sku qty price
  while read -r sku qty price; do
    total=$(( total + qty * price ))
  done < <(each_item "$1")
  cents "$total"
}

# low_stock FILE MIN: skus with qty strictly below MIN, sorted by sku
low_stock() {
  local sku qty price
  each_item "$1" | while read -r sku qty price; do
    if [[ $qty < $2 ]]; then echo "$sku"; fi
  done | sort
}

#!/bin/bash
# collect SRC DEST: move every *.txt regular file directly inside SRC into DEST.
#  - only non-hidden names ending in lowercase ".txt"; directories are skipped
#  - names may contain spaces, glob characters, or start with a dash
#  - DEST/INDEX accumulates every name collect has ever moved into DEST:
#    one name per line, sorted bytewise (LC_ALL=C sort), no duplicates
#  - prints "moved N", N = number of files moved by this run
src=$1
dest=$2
mkdir -p $dest
count=0
for f in $(ls $src | grep '\.txt$'); do
  mv $src/$f $dest/
  echo $f >> $dest/INDEX
  count=$((count + 1))
done
sort -o $dest/INDEX $dest/INDEX
echo "moved $count"

files./home/eval/pipeline/bin/build.sh:
#!/bin/bash
# build.sh: data/sales.csv -> dist/summary.txt (region totals, biggest first,
# ties by region name).
# Contract: if any stage fails, build.sh exits non-zero and dist/summary.txt
# is left exactly as it was. FAIL_STAGE=<stage> injects a failure into that
# stage (extract, transform, validate, publish); the tests rely on it.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

stage() {
  if [ "${FAIL_STAGE:-}" = "$1" ]; then
    echo "injected failure in $1" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

extract() {
  local rows=$(stage extract && grep -v '^#' data/sales.csv | cut -d, -f2,3)
  echo "$rows" > build/extracted.csv
}

transform() {
  stage transform
  awk -F, '{ total[$1] += $2 } END { for (r in total) print r "," total[r] }' \
    build/extracted.csv > build/totals.csv
}

validate() {
  stage validate
  if grep -qv '^[a-z][a-z]*,[0-9][0-9]*$' build/totals.csv; then
    echo "validate: malformed totals" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

publish() {
  mkdir -p dist
  { stage publish && sort -t, -k2,2nr -k1,1 build/totals.csv; } |
    awk -F, '{ printf "%-6s %5d\n", $1, $2 }' > dist/summary.txt
}

main() {
  extract
  if ! transform; then
    echo "transform failed, continuing with previous totals" >&2
  fi
  validate || echo "warning: validation failed" >&2
  publish
}

mkdir -p build

#!/bin/bash
# Failure injection + clean build. See the contract in bin/build.sh.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
mkdir -p dist build
fail=0
for s in extract transform validate publish; do
  printf 'SENTINEL\n' > dist/summary.txt
  if FAIL_STAGE=$s bash bin/build.sh > "build/run-$s.out" 2>&1; then
    echo "FAIL: build.sh exited 0 with FAIL_STAGE=$s"; fail=1
  fi
  if [ "$(cat dist/summary.txt)" != SENTINEL ]; then
    echo "FAIL: dist/summary.txt changed with FAIL_STAGE=$s"; fail=1

  echo "FAIL: clean build exited non-zero"; sed 's/^/    /' build/run-ok.out; fail=1
fi
if ! cmp -s tests/expected-summary.txt dist/summary.txt; then
  echo "FAIL: dist/summary.txt differs from tests/expected-summary.txt"; fail=1
fi
if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo PASS | tee build/test-report.txt
else
  echo FAIL > build/test-report.txt
  exit 1
fi

description: Reconcile quoted CSV vs TSV exports: dedupe, id/date normalisation, exact-cent sums, golden report
prompt:
Reconcile two payment exports in /home/eval/recon: ledger.csv (our books) and bank.tsv (the bank). Write the report to /home/eval/recon/out/reconciliation.txt.

Input rules:
- ledger.csv is RFC 4180 CSV with a header: txn_id,date,payee,amount. Fields may be double-quoted; quoted fields can contain commas and doubled quotes (""). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Amounts may contain thousands separators (e.g. "1,045.50").
- bank.tsv is tab-separated with a header: ref, posted, description, amount. No quoting (a double quote is a literal character). posted is DD/MM/YYYY. ref may have surrounding spaces and any letter case; normalise it by trimming spaces and uppercasing, then it matches ledger txn_id. Amounts may have 0-3 decimal digits (e.g. 2000, 300.1, 89.990).
- All amount comparisons and sums are exact to the cent (never compare floating-point values).
- A bank row whose normalised (ref, date, amount) equals an earlier bank row is a duplicate: drop it and count it. After dropping duplicates every ref is unique.

Report format (exact; ids sorted ascending; amounts with exactly two decimals; dates as YYYY-MM-DD; detail lines indented by two spaces; a section with count 0 has no detail lines):
ledger_rows: <number of ledger data rows>
bank_rows: <number of bank rows after dropping duplicates>
duplicate_bank_rows: <number of dropped duplicates>
ledger_total: <sum of ledger amounts>
bank_total: <sum of bank amounts after dropping duplicates>
matched: <ids present in both files with equal amount AND equal date>
amount_mismatch: <count>
  <id> ledger=<amount> bank=<amount>
date_mismatch: <count>
  <id> ledger=<date> bank=<date>
missing_in_bank: <count>
  <id>
missing_in_ledger: <count>
  <id>

An id present in both files whose amount and date both differ appears in both mismatch sections. Use bash, awk, sed, sort or similar tools (no python).

description: Nearest-rank p50/p95 per normalised endpoint over a 3000-line generated log, filtering, multi-key tie-breaks, top 5
prompt:
/home/eval/logs/access.log is an HTTP access log. Each well-formed line is: <timestamp> <method> <path> <status> <latency>ms, separated by single spaces. Produce /home/eval/logs/out/report.tsv with per-endpoint latency statistics.

Rules:
- Skip lines that do not have exactly those 5 fields or whose latency is not a number followed by "ms" (e.g. truncation markers, or "-" for timed-out requests).
- endpoint = path with any query string ("?..." onwards) removed, then a trailing "/" removed (unless the path is just "/").
- Exclude /healthz and every path under /static/.
- For each endpoint: count = number of requests, p50 and p95 = latency percentiles in ms using the nearest-rank method (sort latencies ascending; the p-th percentile is the value at 1-based position ceil(p/100 * count)), err_permille = floor(1000 * (requests with status >= 500) / count).
- Output: tab-separated, a header line `endpoint	count	p50	p95	err_permille`, then the top 5 endpoints ordered by p95 descending, then count descending, then endpoint ascending (byte order). Integers only, no padding.

description: jq group/rollup with null-vs-missing handling, floor math, latest-name lookup, stable multi-key sorts, multiple output files
prompt:
/home/eval/shop/data/orders.json is an array of shop orders. Build per-customer rollups with jq.

Rules:
- Customer key: .customer.id. Orders whose customer is null or missing belong to the key "guest".
- Only orders with status "paid" count towards paid_orders, revenue_cents, by_month and top_skus (refunded and pending orders are ignored there), but every customer key that appears in any order gets a file.
- Line revenue in cents = floor(qty * unit_cents * (100 - discount_pct) / 100), where a null or missing discount_pct means 0.
- name = .customer.name on that customer's most recent order of any status (by .placed); null for "guest".

Write one file per customer key, /home/eval/shop/out/customers/<key>.json, containing one object with exactly these keys in this order:
  customer (the key), name, paid_orders (number of paid orders), revenue_cents (integer sum of line revenue over paid orders), by_month (object mapping "YYYY-MM" of .placed to that month's revenue, keys ascending, only months with paid orders), top_skus (array of up to 3 skus with the highest revenue over paid orders, ties broken by sku ascending)
Also write /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json: an array of {"customer": <key>, "revenue_cents": <int>} for every customer key, sorted by revenue_cents descending then customer ascending.

Format every file exactly as `jq .` pretty-prints it (2-space indent, one trailing newline). Numbers must be integers (no 12.0).

description: Stale make output: missing script/map prerequisites, hardcoded source list, $^ trap; verified with make -q mtime test
prompt: In the git repository /home/eval/reports, `make` builds build/report.txt from data/*.csv using the awk scripts in lib/ and data/regions.map. After recent commits the report is stale and `make` says there is nothing to do. Fix the Makefile so that build/report.txt is rebuilt whenever anything it is derived from changes, including when a new data/*.csv file is added; `make test` checks this with `make -q` on a scratch copy. Do not edit tests/, lib/ or data/. Then run plain `make` so build/report.txt is current, and commit the Makefile with a message starting with `build:`.

SUMS := build/eu.sum build/us.sum

all: build/report.txt

build/%.sum: data/%.csv
	@mkdir -p build
	awk -F, -f lib/sum.awk $< | sort > $@

build/report.txt: $(SUMS)
	awk -f lib/fmt.awk data/regions.map $^ | sort > $@

test:
	@bash tests/test_deps.sh

.PHONY: all test

#!/bin/bash
# Checks the Makefile dependency graph with `make -q` on a scratch copy:
# touching any input must make build/report.txt out of date.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
t=build/deps-check
inputs="lib/sum.awk lib/fmt.awk data/regions.map data/eu.csv data/us.csv data/apac.csv"
rm -rf "$t"; mkdir -p "$t"
cp -R Makefile lib data "$t"/
make -s -C "$t" build/report.txt > /dev/null || { echo "FAIL: make build/report.txt"; exit 1; }
cmp -s tests/expected-report.txt "$t/build/report.txt" || { echo "FAIL: report differs from tests/expected-report.txt"; exit 1; }

#!/bin/bash
# publish SRC DEST: render the key=value file SRC into DEST as "key: value"
# lines sorted by key (LC_ALL=C byte order). Blank lines and lines starting
# with # are ignored. Every line of SRC counts, even a last line without a
# trailing newline. Values may contain "=".
#
# Contract (tests/test_publish.sh checks all of it):
#   exit 0  success: DEST replaced, nothing printed on stdout
#   exit 2  usage error (not exactly two arguments)
#   exit 3  SRC has a line that is not blank, not a comment and not
#           key=value with key matching [a-z_]+ ; prints
#           "publish: bad line N" (N = 1-based line number) on stderr
#   exit 4  the directory DEST would be written to does not exist
#   On every non-zero exit DEST is left untouched, and on every exit no
#   temporary file or directory remains in ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}.
set -eu

[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "usage: publish SRC DEST" >&2; exit 1; }
src=$1 dest=$2

render() {
  local tmp=$(mktemp)
  local work=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
  n=0
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    case $line in
      ''|'#'*) continue ;;
      [a-z_]*=*) echo "$line" >> "$work/pairs" ;;
      *) echo "publish: bad line $n" >&2; exit 3 ;;
    esac
  done < "$src"
  sort "$work/pairs" | sed 's/=/: /' > "$tmp"
  cp "$tmp" "$dest"
}

render
trap 'echo "publish: done"; exit 0' EXIT
